intro: This is a preview. Everything on it was computed, written and checked by AI models within two days; no person has checked it. The checks below were made on the data shown on these pages.

checks.name: Substitution of every listed solution
checks.what: Each closed form in a list is substituted into its equation by a second program that shares no code with the engine: exactly where possible, otherwise numerically to 30 digits (20 for the largest formulas) at random points of the parameter values for which the solution is stated.
checks.result: 2446 solutions pass exactly, 516 pass numerically, 0 failed (a failed item is removed and the verdict lowered), 212 could not be checked (no random point of the locus found, or no closed form; for 87 of them the check was inconclusive or stopped with an error).

checks.name: Published classifications as a test
checks.what: Sixty complete classifications taken from the literature (233 solutions in all) are used as a test set: the engine is run on each equation without access to the answer, and its list is compared with the published one.
checks.result: 229 of the 233 solutions are found (two of them only when the equation is analysed alone; in a batch on a busy machine their search runs out of time). In the cases where one is not found, the report itself says that its list is not complete.

checks.name: Symbolic answers against numeric ones
checks.what: For reports with parameters that say that every meromorphic solution is listed, the equation is solved again at numeric values of the parameters (generic points, points where a parameter vanishes, points on the conditions of each listed family; about one thousand instances in each round), and the two lists are compared. A separate search generated about 4500 special parameter points for the first- and second-order equations from the algebra of each equation (vanishing coefficients, multiple roots, integer indices) and compared the answers there.
checks.result: The differences found in the first rounds were traced to their causes and corrected. In the last rounds no nonconstant solution was missing inside a stated scope; the last round found constant solutions missing on special parameter values in five reports, and they are listed now.

checks.name: Two procedures for the same equations
checks.what: Equations of the form A(w) w'' + B(w) w'^2 + C(w) = 0 are decided by two programs written independently; a report says "complete" only when they give the same set of functions.
checks.result: Where they differ the union is shown and completeness is not claimed.

checks.name: Second reading of proofs and programs
checks.what: Each statement labelled agent-proof was written by one AI model and read by another, which also tested the program that applies it with equations whose solutions are known.
checks.result: Every reading found something to correct in a program, and the corrections are in; the proofs themselves stood. The registry page says for each statement whether it has had a second reading.

checks.name: Reading of the input
checks.what: The reductions of the catalogue's evolution equations to travelling-wave equations were derived again by an independent program, and typed inputs in unusual notation (LaTeX, equation numbers, words around the equation, coefficients written next to the unknown) were tried in five rounds.
checks.result: The reductions agree. Every round found ways in which a typed equation could be read differently from what was meant; those found were closed: the page now refuses such input or shows a warning that says how it was read. More such ways may exist: check the line "read as" under the input box, and prefer plain notation such as w'' = 6*w^2 + a or u_t + 6*u*u_x + u_xxx = 0.

checks.name: Regression tests
checks.what: Every defect found by a check became a test case of the engine (one hundred cases for the report level alone, with about thirty properties tested on every report); they are run before each build.
checks.result: All pass on the present build.

limits: "Complete" is a statement about solutions that are meromorphic in the whole complex plane, and it is as strong as the statements it rests on: the label next to each verdict names the weakest of them. For most equations this is an agent-level proof that no person has read.
"Complete for generic parameters" says nothing about the special parameter values listed under "not decided", except for the solutions that are listed there.

For an evolution equation the statements are about the reduced ordinary differential equation shown on the page, under the conditions stated with the reduction (for instance an integration constant set to zero).
The same function can still appear twice in a list in different forms.

The engine in the browser works without the algebra programs of the full version and under a time limit: typed equations with several parameters can get a weaker answer than the catalogue entry of the same equation.
If a step of the analysis does not end in the browser, the page stops it, repeats the analysis without that step and says so; the answer can then be weaker than the full one, never stronger.
